items.prompt: Which body part do we use to walk?

options.why: Ears help us hear. They do not help us walk.
Elbows help our arms bend.

hints: Think about what moves when you walk.
Stand up and take a step. What moves?
March on the spot and notice which parts lift up.
items.explanation: We use our legs and feet to walk, run and jump.

items.prompt: Match each body part to what it helps us do.
hints: Think about using each body part.
Do the easy ones first.
Take a bite of food in your mind. Which part chews?
items.explanation: Teeth chew food, legs help us walk and run, hands hold things and the neck lets us turn our head.

items.prompt: How many eyes do most people have?
hints: Look at a face in a mirror.
Count one eye, then the other.
Point to your left eye and say 1.
items.explanation: Most people have 2 eyes, one on each side of the nose.

items.prompt: Which body part is between your hand and your shoulder?

options.why: Your knee is in the middle of your leg.
Your ankle joins your foot to your leg.

hints: Touch your shoulder, then slide down to your hand.
Find the place where your arm bends.
Bend your arm and look at the pointy part.
items.explanation: The elbow is in the middle of the arm, between the shoulder and the hand. It lets the arm bend.

items.prompt: Your leg bends in the middle. What is that part called?

options.why: Your wrist joins your hand to your arm.
Your neck holds up your head.

hints: Sit down and look at your legs.
Find where your leg bends when you sit.
Put your hand on the bend in your leg.
items.explanation: The knee is in the middle of the leg. It lets the leg bend when we sit, kick or climb.

items.prompt: Where is each body part? Sort the cards.
hints: Think about where each part is on your body.
Touch each part on yourself as you sort.
Start with your elbow. Is it on your arm or your leg?
items.explanation: The elbow, wrist and fingers are on the arm and hand. The knee, ankle and toes are on the leg and foot.

items.prompt: We chew our food with our ___.

figure.alt: A picture of a body part that is hard and white, with a question mark.

hints: Think about eating a crunchy apple.
Which parts in your mouth are hard and white?
Run your tongue along the inside of your mouth.
items.explanation: We chew food with our teeth. Brushing them keeps them clean and strong.

items.prompt: Where do people wear a watch?

options.why: A necklace goes around the neck. A watch goes on the arm.
The knee is on the leg. A watch goes on the arm.

hints: Picture someone checking the time on a watch.
Which part of the arm is thin and near the hand?
Look at where your hand joins your arm.
items.explanation: A watch is worn on the wrist. The wrist joins the hand to the arm.

items.prompt: Choose all the body parts that come in pairs.

options.why: Most people have one nose, in the middle of the face.
Most people have one mouth.

hints: A pair means two of the same thing.
Count each one on your own body.
Start with your eyes. How many are there?
items.explanation: Eyes, ears and arms come in pairs, one on each side of the body. The nose and mouth are in the middle, and there is one of each.

items.prompt: Order the body parts from the top to the bottom.
hints: Start at the very top of your body.
Touch each part as you go down.
Put the head first, then find the part just below it.
items.explanation: From top to bottom, the order is head, neck, shoulders, knees, ankles and toes.

items.prompt: Which body part helps us taste, eat and talk?

figure.alt: Three pictures: a nose, an ear and a tongue.

options.why: The nose helps us smell and breathe. It does not help us chew.
Ears help us hear. They do not help us eat.

hints: Think about what moves in your mouth when you speak.
Which part is inside your mouth?
Say la la la slowly. What moves?
items.explanation: The tongue helps us taste food, move it around while we chew and make sounds when we talk.

items.prompt: Some body parts are inside us. Which one is inside?

options.why: You can see your elbow on the outside of your arm.
Your chin is on the outside, at the bottom of your face.

hints: Think about parts you can feel but not see.
Put your hand on your chest. What can you feel beating?
Check each one. Can you see it in a mirror?
items.explanation: The heart is inside the chest. We cannot see it, but we can feel it beating. The elbow and the chin are on the outside.

items.prompt: Choose all the places where your body can bend.

options.why: The nose does not bend like a joint.
The chin does not bend. The jaw below it moves to open the mouth.

hints: A bend lets part of your body fold.
Gently try moving each part.
Start with your elbow. Can your arm fold there?
items.explanation: The elbow, the knee and the wrist are joints. Joints are places where the body bends. The nose and the chin do not bend.

items.prompt: Draw yourself on paper. Label your head, arm and leg. Then take a photo.
items.explanation: Your tutor checks that you drew a body and labelled three parts.

items.prompt: Tap the head.

figure.alt: A child standing with arms out to the sides. The picture shows the head, arms, hands, tummy, legs and feet.

hints: Look at the top of the body.
Your eyes, nose and mouth are here.
You wear a hat on it.
items.explanation: The head is at the top of the body. It has the eyes, nose, mouth and ears.

items.prompt: Tap the part that you stand on.

figure.alt: A child standing with arms out to the sides. The picture shows the head, arms, hands, tummy, legs and feet.

hints: Look at the bottom of the body.
You put a shoe on it.
It is at the end of the leg.
items.explanation: The foot is at the end of the leg. We stand and walk on our feet.

items.prompt: Tap the arm.

figure.alt: A child standing with arms out to the sides. The picture shows the head, arms, hands, tummy, legs and feet.

hints: You use this part to wave and to carry things.
It is at the side of the body.
It joins the shoulder to the hand.
items.explanation: The arm is at the side of the body. We use our arms to carry, reach and wave.

items.prompt: Label the parts of the body.

figure.alt: A child standing with arms out to the sides. The picture shows the head, arms, hands, tummy, legs and feet.

hints: Tap a label, then tap its number.
The head is at the top.
The foot is at the bottom of the leg.
items.explanation: The head is at the top, the arm is at the side, the leg is below the body and the foot is at the end of the leg.

items.prompt: Label the parts of the body. One label is not needed.

figure.alt: A child standing with arms out to the sides. The picture shows the head, arms, hands, tummy, legs and feet.

hints: Tap a label, then tap its number.
Your hand is at the end of your arm.
Your tummy is in the middle of your body.
items.explanation: The labels are head, hand, tummy and foot. The knee is not needed.

items.prompt: What do we have at the end of each hand?

options.why: Toes are on our feet.
An elbow is the bend in the arm.

hints: Look at your hand.
You write with them.
Toes are on feet.
items.explanation: Each hand has five fingers.

items.prompt: Which part of the body is at the top?

options.why: The knee is in the leg.
The foot is at the bottom.

hints: Think about where your hat goes.
The foot is not at the top.
Look at the top of your body.
items.explanation: The head is at the top of the body.

items.prompt: Which part joins your hand to your arm?

options.why: The knee is in the leg.
The neck joins the head and the body.

hints: Where do you wear a watch?
It is a joint in your arm.
It is next to your hand.
items.explanation: The wrist is the bendy part between the hand and the arm.

items.prompt: How many toes do you have on one foot?
hints: Look at your foot.
Count each toe.
Count slowly.
items.explanation: Most people have five toes on each foot.

items.prompt: Top half or bottom half of the body? Sort the cards.
hints: Your legs are in the bottom half.
Your head is at the top.
Start with the knee.
items.explanation: The head, hand and shoulder are in the top half. The knee, foot and toe are in the bottom half.

items.prompt: Is it outside or inside the body? Sort the cards.
hints: Can you see it in the mirror?
Bones are under the skin.
Start with the skin.
items.explanation: We can see our skin, hair and nose. The brain, bones and stomach are inside us.

items.prompt: Choose all the parts of the face.
hints: Look in a mirror.
Your face has the parts you see with.
An elbow is on the arm.
items.explanation: Eyes, nose and mouth are on the face. The elbow, knee and toe are not.

items.prompt: Match each body part to what you wear.
hints: Think where each one goes.
A glove has fingers.
A hat sits on the top.
items.explanation: We wear a hat on the head and a shoe on the foot. A glove goes on the hand and a scarf goes on the neck.

items.prompt: Order the parts of the arm. Start at the shoulder.
hints: The shoulder is near the neck.
The fingers are at the end.
The wrist is next to the hand.
items.explanation: An arm starts at the shoulder. Then come the elbow, the wrist and the fingers.

items.prompt: Order the parts of the leg. Start at the hip.
hints: The hip is at the top.
The toes are at the end.
The ankle is above the foot.
items.explanation: A leg starts at the hip. Then come the knee, the ankle and the toes.

items.prompt: We walk with our ___. We hold a pencil with our ___.
hints: What do you use to walk?
What do you use to write?
Read each sentence.
items.explanation: We walk with our legs and we hold a pencil with our hands.

items.prompt: How many do we have?
head: Body part
How many?
hints: Look in a mirror.
Count your ears.
You have one nose.
items.explanation: We have two eyes, one nose, two ears and one mouth.

items.prompt: Kim runs in the park. She kicks a ball with her foot. She waves to a friend with her hand. She smiles with her mouth.

parts.prompt: What does Kim kick the ball with?

hints: Read the second sentence.
Which part kicks?
The third sentence tells about waving.
items.explanation: Kim kicks with her foot and waves with her hand.

items.prompt: Tap the foot.

figure.alt: A child standing with arms out to the sides. The picture shows the head, arms, hands, tummy, legs and feet.

hints: You stand on it.
It is at the bottom.
It is below the leg.
items.explanation: The foot is at the bottom of the leg. We stand on our feet.

items.prompt: Tap the tummy.

figure.alt: A child standing with arms out to the sides. The picture shows the head, arms, hands, tummy, legs and feet.

hints: It is in the middle.
Your food goes here.
It is below the neck.
items.explanation: The tummy is the middle part of the body, between the chest and the legs.

items.prompt: Label the child. One label does not belong.

figure.alt: A child standing with arms out to the sides. The picture shows the head, arms, hands, tummy, legs and feet.

hints: Start at the top.
Birds have wings.
The foot is at the bottom.
items.explanation: A child has a head, a tummy, legs and feet. A child does not have a wing.

items.prompt: You have ten fingers and ten ___.
hints: Look at your feet.
Fingers are on hands.
It starts with t.
items.explanation: We have ten fingers on our hands and ten toes on our feet.

items.prompt: Draw a face with eyes, a nose and a mouth. Add two ears.

criteria.label: Draws two eyes, a nose and a mouth

hints: Start with a round face.
Put the eyes above the nose.
items.explanation: A face has two eyes, one nose, one mouth and two ears.

items.prompt: You run, jump and kick. Which body parts do you use for all three?

options.why: Arms do not kick.
Ears do not help us run.
Eyes help us see, not kick.

hints: Which part moves when you run?
Which part kicks a ball?
It is in the bottom half.
items.explanation: We use our legs to run, jump and kick.

items.prompt: Kai has 2 hands. Each hand has 5 fingers. How many fingers does Kai have in all?
hints: Count one hand.
There are two hands.
Add 5 and 5.
items.explanation: 5 fingers on each hand and 2 hands make 10 fingers.

items.prompt: Four friends take off both shoes. Each foot has 5 toes. How many toes can you count?
hints: First find the toes on one friend.
One friend has 10 toes.
Add 10 four times.
items.explanation: Each friend has 2 feet with 5 toes. That is 10 toes each. 4 friends have 40 toes.
